title: Logistics Coordinator

title: Senior AI Security Engineer

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing - and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara is building a brand-new role at the intersection of security engineering and applied AI. This person will be the most AI-forward technologist on our Application Security team - using frontier AI models to both strengthen our security posture and stress-test it. You'll spend one day using AI to red-team our cloud environment and the next validating firmware vulnerabilities on our hardware, with the goal to secure our applications for AI Adversaries. This is a highly visible, org-wide role reporting into a newly formed function, with a clear path to shape Samsara's AI security strategy for years to come.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

• You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.

• You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

• Deliver accurate, consistent security assessments of Samsara's software, code,  and firmware, evaluating their resilience against AI-driven/adversarial attacks, and implementing fixes.

• Build and pressure-test novel AI-enabled security tooling and workflows, then drive adoption of what proves valuable across the broader security org.

• Genuinely curious about AI and able to speak credibly about what we're building

title: Sales Representative (m/w/d) - Berlin
description:
Du hast erste Vertriebserfahrung und willst jetzt richtig loslegen? Bei uns bekommst du ein strukturiertes Onboarding, dein eigenes Gebiet, kurze Sales-Cycles und ein Team, das dich weiterentwickelt.

Salonkee ist Marktführer für Salon-Software in Luxemburg, Belgien und der Schweiz. Über 10.000 Beauty- und Wellness-Betriebe in sieben Ländern nutzen unsere All-in-one-Software - von der Terminbuchung über die Kundenverwaltung und die Kasse bis hin zu Marketing- und KI-Funktionen.

Für einen Salon bedeutet das im Schnitt 70% weniger Terminausfälle und 8 bis 12 Stunden weniger Verwaltungsaufwand pro Woche.

DEINE ROLLE

- Du verantwortest das Wachstum in deiner Region und bist die zentrale Ansprechperson vor Ort

- Du gehst aktiv auf Saloninhaber:innen in deiner Region zu - telefonisch, per Walk-in oder über Social Media (Kaltakquise).

- Vor Ort ermittelst du den Bedarf des Salons mithilfe von Fragen und zeigst anhand von Produktdemos, wie Salonkee den Alltag vereinfachen kann.

- Du verantwortest deinen eigenen Funnel vom Erstkontakt bis zum Abschluss.

- Deine Woche planst du eigenverantwortlich, mit klaren Zielen und einer Führungskraft, die dich unterstützt und weiterentwickelt.

DAS BRINGST DU MIT

- Nachweisbare erste Erfahrung im Vertrieb, idealerweise mit Outbound-Anteil (Kaltakquise, Walk-ins, eigene Terminierung).

- Du bist kontaktfreudig und gehst gerne in den Austausch - egal ob am Telefon oder direkt vor Ort.

- Du bist in der Lage, Menschen zu begeistern und Interessen zu wecken.

- Du kannst mit Ablehnung umgehen und richtest den Blick nach vorn.

- Du bist lernbereit, setzt Feedback um und willst dich weiterentwickeln.

- Du bist strukturiert, organisiert und sicher im Umgang mit digitalen Tools.

- Verhandlungssicheres bis muttersprachliches Deutsch sowie gute Englischkenntnisse.

- Führerschein der Klasse B und Freude daran, in deiner Region unterwegs zu sein.

DAS ERWARTET DICH BEI UNS

- Ein Team vor Ort: Team Lead und Kolleg:innen in deiner Region - du startest nicht allein.

- Strukturierte Einarbeitung und praxisnahe Begleitung über die ersten Monate hinweg (Ramp-Up Programm).

- Ein klarer Entwicklungspfad: Von Junior über Senior bis hin zu Führungsrollen.

- Klare KPIs & Performance-Transparenz, damit du jederzeit weißt, wo du stehst.

- Eigenverantwortliche Wochenplanung und Vertrauensarbeitszeit.

- Firmenwagen inkl. Tankkarte sowie MacBook und iPhone.

- 50 € steuerfreies Guthaben pro Monat über Probonio.

- Fixgehalt und ungedeckelte Provision.

- Teamevents, die ihren Namen verdienen: Sommerfest, Winterfeier und regelmäßige Teamformate.

WIE GEHT ES WEITER?

1. Bewerbung & Sichtung - wir melden uns so schnell wie möglich bei dir.

2. Erstgespräch mit unserem Recruiting-Team (ca. 30-45 Minuten).

3. Video-Call mit deiner künftigen Führungskraft.

4. Field Day - zwei Stunden bei uns im Office. Du siehst, wie wir arbeiten, wir sehen dich in Aktion.

5. Abschlussgespräch mit unserer Head of Sales.

Salonkee steht für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, Perspektiven und Fähigkeiten - unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Alter, Behinderung, Religion oder Identität.

title: Senior Covenant Lawyer - Distressed
description:
About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets - the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

THE OPPORTUNITY

9fin is looking for a corporate finance attorney who geeks out about a good credit agreement or indenture and who has broader ambitions to write and be a thought-leader in the industry they love. This role will help our distressed editorial teams understand all the nuances of interesting bond and loan documents that could factor into restructuring and liability management exercises. It is perfect for an experienced finance attorney who is looking to recalibrate their work-life balance to allow for a little more life, but who loves their work. We’re growing our groundbreaking coverage of complex out-of-court restructurings with an emphasis on distressed coverage. The role will report into our New York office with flexibility to work from home / remotely as needed.

This role offers a unique opportunity for a legal professional to use their expertise within a rapidly growing start-up environment, with opportunities to refine an already valuable skillset while learning all of the new skills that comes with working with technologists, credit analysts and journalists.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

Every day is different, but here’s an example of the kind of things you’ll work on:

- Reviewing leveraged finance and high yield documentation to produce commercially focused and insightful analysis on distressed scenarios and the primary market

- Writing topical reports on secondary situations, collaborating closely across 9fin’s team of lawyers and credit analysts

- Answering client questions about the covenant packages of specific borrowers and issuers

- Using 9fin’s proprietary technology to build and expand our restructuring and LME databases

- Delivering seminars, teach-ins and podcast segments as a subject matter expert

- Representing 9fin in the press and at industry conferences and events

ABOUT YOU

This role will be a great fit if you have the following:

- JD with 5+ years of experience within a capital solutions, leveraged finance, capital markets, restructuring and/or special situations team at a top-tier law firm

- Experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating high yield bond and/or leveraged loan documents, restructuring support agreements, and Chapter 11 documentation

- Keen commercial awareness of leveraged finance and restructuring markets

- Strong technical understanding of how leveraged finance covenants and definitions operate

- Existing network of relationships within the leveraged finance community

- Excellent relationship building skills

- Effective written and verbal communication skills, able to explain complex covenant concepts to non-lawyers concisely

- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively

 

OUR BENEFITS

We’re a scaling start up and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Financial & Insurance

- Equity

- 401(k) (9fin pay 3%, employee contributions are uncapped)

title: Vendor Security Technical Program Manager
description:
About the Team

OpenAI's Vendor Security team helps internal teams work securely with external products, services, and partners. Our work spans software, infrastructure, hardware, professional and managed services, vendor-provided workforces, data, and research. We build the programs and products that help teams understand vendor risk and put effective safeguards in place, protecting our customers, employees, and the company.

About the Role

We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work.

You will independently lead vendor-security engagements: understand the business need, investigate the actual data and access, recommend a practical path, and work with the responsible owners until the safeguards are verified. You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead.

This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. You should be comfortable taking a position, explaining the tradeoff, and changing your mind when the evidence changes. Success means internal teams can use vendors securely, reuse work that still applies, and understand what needs to happen next.

In this role, you will:

- Own vendor security engagements from understanding the business need through scoping, assessment, decision, treatment, and reassessment when material facts change. Make assessment decisions independently and use judgment about when to involve peers, specialists, or leadership. Route formal exceptions and risk acceptance to the appropriate decision owners.

- Understand vendor use cases, workflows, user journeys, data flows, identities, access, integrations, and supply-chain dependencies. Identify plausible attack paths and their consequences for OpenAI.

- Assess relevant architectures, configurations, controls, logs, and operational practices. Test whether the evidence supports the security claims that matter to the engagement, and make gaps and uncertainty clear.

- Develop practical treatments, including changes to the operating model, data exposure, access, architecture, vendor choice, controls, or containment. Drive implementation with the responsible owners and verify that the treatment works.

- Build reusable security patterns with clear applicability, safeguards, evidence requirements, exceptions, and review triggers.

- Work with Legal, Procurement, and vendors on security addenda. Evaluate proposed terms and deviations against the engagement, explain their security implications, and develop workable positions with the appropriate decision owners. Legal leads wording and negotiation.

- Learn from internal customers, agree priorities with the Vendor Security lead, and define the requirements, roadmap, and success measures for the bounded programs, products, and services you own.

- Use Codex or comparable AI-assisted tools to build, inspect, test, and maintain practical improvements to scoping, evidence checks, routing, decision reuse, or treatment tracking. Investigate failures and own the result through adoption, continued operation, and explicit handoff or retirement.

- Lead delivery across Security and partner teams. Translate goals into technical requirements, milestones, and delivery plans; influence implementation choices; identify systemic risks; resolve dependencies and disagreements; and carry commitments through completion.

- Use casework, incidents, threat information, and customer feedback to improve decisions and the program. As priorities change, recommend what to do next and explain the tradeoffs and effects on existing commitments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have independently assessed consequential third-party, supply-chain, or comparable security risks, and can apply that judgment to unfamiliar vendor technologies and operating model

title: Security Engineer, Incident Response
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

THE SECURITY TEAM

- Examples of key problems the team is working on

- You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

- Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

- Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.

ROLE SCOPE

- Lead incident response end to end across corporate, cloud, and data center environments, from detection and containment through eradication and post-incident review.

- Build the detection logic, response playbooks, and forensic tooling for an environment where the assets under threat are the most targeted model weights in technology.

- Run investigations across a threat surface measured in gigawatts, correlating signals from cloud, endpoint, network, and physical systems into a single picture of an attack.

- Stand up the incident response function from the ground up, defining severity models, on-call rotations, and the escalation path to leadership.

- Turn each incident into a permanent improvement by partnering with the security and IT teams to close the gaps your investigations surface.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c.

- You've personally led major security incidents from first alert to resolution, making containment calls under pressure with the business watching.

- You've built detection logic and response playbooks that caught real intrusions, not just theoretical ones.

- You've run digital forensics across cloud, endpoint, and network evidence and reconstructed what an attacker actually did.

- You've stood up or substantially rebuilt an incident response program rather than only operating inside someone else's.

title: Sr. Information Security Risk Analyst
description:
We are hiring a Senior Information Security Risk Analyst on our Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team!

In this role, you will serve as a technical subject matter expert in application security risk management, leading governance and oversight of our SAST/DAST application security scanning program, including static and dynamic application security testing. You will assess security vulnerabilities, evaluate findings from application and infrastructure scanning tools, and partner with application teams, incident management teams, and business stakeholders to prioritize and remediate risk. A key focus will be maximizing the value of the SAST/DAST platform, strengthening vulnerability management practices, improving risk visibility, and translating technical findings into actionable business risk insights. Successful candidates will bring strong expertise in application security testing, vulnerability management, and risk assessment, with hands-on experience using SAST/DAST platforms, a proven ability to drive remediation efforts, and a CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or comparable security certification.
Additionally, this role serves to support a high-visibility Data Governance initiative where you will help shape how enterprise data is governed, protected, and leveraged across the organization. You will partner with business leaders, data owners, security, privacy, compliance, and technology teams to establish governance standards, assess risk, monitor compliance, and strengthen data stewardship practices. This role provides the opportunity to influence enterprise-wide decisions and advance a mature Data Governance program. Successful candidates will be skilled relationship builders who can translate complex governance and regulatory requirements into practical business processes, drive accountability for data quality and policy adherence, and effectively balance regulatory expectations with business objectives.
Experience supporting SOC 2 audits, NIST frameworks and SSP development, third-party risk management, governance activities, and communicating complex security risks to both technical and non-technical audiences is highly valued. Strong collaboration, relationship-building, and influencing skills are essential, as this role will work across multiple teams to strengthen the organization's security posture.

Note:

• Participation in on-call rotation is required for two weeks every 22 weeks.

• Must be able to work Eastern Time business hours.

• This is a remote, work-from-home position, but the final round of interviews will take place on-site in our Chattanooga, TN office.

• Sponsorship is not available for this role.

Job Responsibilities

•
Lead SOC 2 Audit Support - Coordinate audit activities including evidence collection, control validation, and auditor engagement.

•
Manage and Validate Control Frameworks - Maintain control documentation, mappings, and narratives while partnering with control owners to ensure effectiveness and alignment with Trust Services Criteria and NIST frameworks.

•
Track Audit & Remediation Activities - Oversee audit findings, remediation efforts, and timely closure of issues.

•
Develop & Maintain NIST SSPs - Create and update System Security Plans (SSPs), including control implementations, inheritance, and system boundaries.

•
Drive Security Awareness Programs - Design and manage training initiatives, including phishing simulations and targeted campaigns.

•
Manage Policies & Governance Documentation - Oversee the full lifecycle of security policies, standards, and procedures to ensure compliance and audit readiness.

•
Conduct Enterprise & Third-Party Risk Management - Perform risk assessments, maintain risk registers, execute vendor risk assessments, and monitor remediation.

•
Oversee Vulnerability Management - Track vulnerability remediation against SLAs and collaborate with teams to mitigate risks.

•
Support Customer Security Assurance - Respond to RFPs and security questionnaires,

title: Sr. Mechanical Engineer
description:
Who We Are:

Aurelius Systems is a VC backed defense tech startup building autonomous, edge deployed directed energy systems for counter-UAS. We build laser weapons to shoot down drones.

We're a small team of engineers, former US military, and subject matter experts scaling America's directed energy dominance. The first cost effective, reliable and robust laser weapon system.

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing. That's how we operate small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we opened our Detroit manufacturing hub and field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

The Role and Your Impact:

We need a Senior Mechanical Engineer who owns major mechanical subsystems on Archimedes end to end and makes them survive the field. That means ruggedization of a fiber laser system against shock, vibration, moisture and environmental extremes, plus the structure, thermal management and precision packaging around the laser head and beam director. You'll work hands on from architecture through bench validation, field correlation and the production handoff to our Detroit manufacturing hub, alongside our Staff and Principal engineers.

What You'll Own:

- Mechanical design of major subsystems: laser source and head enclosures, gimbal and beam director structure, mounts

- Survivability to MIL-STD shock, vibration, humidity, dust and austere environments

- Thermal management for high-power laser and electronics packaging

- Precision and optomechanical packaging that holds alignment through shock and thermal cycles

- FEA (static, modal, random vibration, shock response spectrum) and correlation to test

- Test rigs, instrumentation and bench validation you build and run yourself

- DFM and the handoff to manufacturing in Detroit

- Design reviews and raising the bar for the junior ME team

What We're Looking For:

- 5+ years in mechanical engineering on ruggedized, field-deployable or high-performance systems

- At least one subsystem you took from prototype to production

- Strong FEA (ANSYS, Nastran, Abaqus or equivalent) and the bench work to back it up

- Hands-on design to MIL-STD-810 or equivalent shock and vibration standards

- Thermal design for high-power systems

- Evidence you learn fast. You got effective in a new domain in months, not years

Where you probably come from: Defense hardware, airborne or ground vehicle systems, F1 and high-performance automotive, aerospace, maritime, ruggedized electronics, or directed energy and field-deployed sensor programs. Domain matters less than shipping hardware that had to survive.

We want to talk if: You've owned a system that had to survive shock, vibration and environmental extremes in a tight, deployable package, and you modeled it, built it, instrumented it and correlated it.

Not a fit if: You've only done commercial or consumer product design, your work is simulation-only with no bench validation, or you've spent years on one narrow subcomponent without seeing the system around it.

Nice to Haves:

- Laser, directed energy or high-power hardware

- Optical bench or precision instrument ruggedization

- MIL-STD-461 EMI/EMC awareness for mechanical integration

- Vehicle-mounted systems

- Manufacturing ramp experience

Education: BS or MS in Mechanical, Aerospace or related field. What you've built matters more than where you went to school.

How You Operate:

- Extreme bias for action. You'd rather build a prototype tomorrow than model it for a month

- You characterize your own systems before the field does

- Comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration in a startup environment

- You debug from first principles, not intuition alone

- Clear communicator across mechanical, electrical, optical, and software teams

- Self directed. You identify what needs to happe

title: RFP: Human Resource Subject Matter Lead

description:
About NLA and TCS

New Left Accelerator (NLA) and its 501(c)(3) affiliate, The Capacity Shop (TCS), lead operational capacity-building programs that empower social justice organizations and movements to execute bold work safely. We bridge the gap between ambitious strategy and operational excellence, scaling structures and impact without sacrificing legal compliance or integrity. To achieve systemic change, organizations must use every tool in their toolbox effectively-including multi-entity structures.

Through deep collaboration with field experts, we build the financial and compliance training systems that allow movement organizations to manage risk and remain resilient. Our work is rooted in a commitment to:

•
Power Building For Systemic Change: Equipping organizations to build power to dismantle oppressive structures.

•
Operational Power: Building the "operational" capacity to execute bold work and to strategically manage risk.

•
A Multi-Entity Lens: Optimizing the diverse legal structures necessary to win critical battles.

•
Transformative Partnerships: Prioritizing those working at the intersections of race, gender, and class.

At NLA, our work is guided by a Theory of Change. We accompany organizations and movements in building sustainable, resilient ecosystems prepared to win the most ambitious fights of our time.

Overview of Project

Background

NLA and TCS develop training on a range of operations topics, focused on what multi-entity organizations need to know. We are developing foundational content for a training module for HR staff at mid-size, multi-entity social justice organizations that do election-year work. The content will focus on the HR issues specific to these organizations when they hire for organizing positions during an election cycle and then end those positions afterward.

Scope of Work

The HR Subject Matter Lead will work under the direction of the TCS, Senior Director of Training and Curriculum to develop a four-part, role-based education module for HR specialists. The module will:

• Apply a nonprofit multi-entity Human Resources lens throughout

• Apply a social justice lens to HR in the organizing and election year context

• Build on existing NLA/TCS content

• Incorporate NLA's learning frameworks and practices

• Be customizable for state content

Deliverables and Outcomes

December 2026 through June 2027

•
Content Audit Report: An assessment of existing NLA/TCS HR content that sorts it into what can be used as is, what needs updating, and what's missing. It will include recommendations for the Content Lead.

•

Accounting Clerk (Accounts Payable / Accounts Receivable)

About the role:
We are seeking a detail-oriented Accounting Clerk to join our Accounting team. This role focuses on Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable, on vendor and dealer administration. You will manage vendor billings and dealer invoices, and ensure all expenses are accurately recorded and reconciled. You will play a key role in maintaining accurate financial records in Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable, supporting month-end close, and strengthening internal controls.
The purpose of the Accounting Clerk is to efficiently manage the processing of vendor invoices for Accounts Payable, as well as generating invoices to dealers in Accounts Receivable. This position supports the day-to-day financial operations of the business, ensuring timely and accurate postings.

• Ability to speak fluent English

• Ability to read and write in English

• Strong attention to detail

• Computer

• Great multitasker

What you’ll Do

Accounts Payable

• Accurately and timely processing of invoices on a daily basis with the correct GL CODE.

• Maintain up to date Vendor records (maintain and organize digital records)

• Process all online bills for monthly payment (hydro, utilities, internet, Waste Connections, etc).

• Assist in any accounting related activities, including year end audit, as required.

What’s in it for you?

• ₱355 to ₱445 Philippine Pesos (PHP) per hour

• Experience within a rapidly growing company

• Remote work

Vi is the market-leading Enterprise-AI platform for health, serving the world’s largest health organizations - from Fortune 500 health providers to pharma and consumer brands - helping them maximize patient activation, engagement, operational excellence and health outcomes. Vi offers four main product lines: Activate, Engage, Operate and Pulse. Backed by $125M+ in R&D, our powerful platform serves over 190 million members daily - and growing. Role Summary
The Director, Strategy & Insights sits at the intersection of science and commercial strategy within Vi ’s Pharma vertical, translating complex scientific, behavioral, and market inputs into sharp, executive-level insights, strategies, and action plans that drive real outcomes for Fortune 500 biopharma clients. This is a senior individual contributor role with ownership of a dedicated book of accounts, built for someone who is as comfortable in the data as they are in the boardroom, moves fast, and holds a genuinely high bar for everything they put their name on. You’ll be the expert voice on every client call and work across Vi ’s data, deployment, marketing, and product teams to bring insights to life.
What You’ll Do

• Own a dedicated book of biopharma accounts as the senior strategic partner, serving as the expert voice across every client interaction

• Lead insight development from strategic question through executive-level client delivery, including decks, targeting strategies, and insight frameworks

• Translate complex scientific, behavioral, and market dynamics into clear, differentiated POVs and action plans that directly inform client commercial decisions

• Act as a trusted strategic partner to VP and C-suite stakeholders at Fortune 500 companies

• Operate across therapeutic areas and drug modalities with confidence, including pre-approval contexts such as clinical trial recruitment and disease state education, and post-approval work including precision marketing and HCP segmentation

• Identify growth opportunities across your accounts, bringing forward strategic recommendations and expansion paths before being asked

• Partner across data science, deployment, marketing, product/tech, and account management to embed insights across the client relationship and the Vi platform

What You’ll Bring
Scientific Depth and Commercial Fluency

• Deep scientific literacy across disease states, MOA, and clinical data, with the ability to credibly engage pharma clients on complex scientific and strategic questions

• Strong commercial instincts and a clear understanding of how insights translate into go-to-market decisions, HCP targeting, and patient engagement strategy

Senior Pharma Insights Experience

• 8+ years of relevant experience in pharma across strategy consulting, insights, medical communications, or agency, with a track record of independently leading client-facing engagements

• Hands-on experience with claims and intent data across HCP and patient audiences, plus competitive intelligence across multiple therapeutic areas

• Primary market research experience a plus

Ownership and Startup Mentality

• Demonstrated track record of owning client relationships and work end to end, not just advising on strategy but building, delivering, and iterating on the final product

• Commercial curiosity: spots where a client relationship can grow and acts on it

• Comfortable working across disciplines and with non-pharma partners, including engineers, marketers, and data scientists

• Entrepreneurial and energized by ambiguity; comfortable without a playbook and managing multiple accounts at speed

• Collaborative, low-ego, and genuinely obsessed with client outcomes

title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

- Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

- Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

- Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

- Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

- Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

- Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk.

- Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates.

- Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines.

- Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs.

- Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions.

title: Head of Engineering (f/m/d)
description:
At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions.

Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next.

We're hiring a Head of Engineering to lead engineering for one of our product tribes. You'll manage 15 to 20 engineers directly, with tech leads in each squad owning technical direction but no management layer between you and the team. You report to the CTO and sit in a tribe leadership trio with the Product Tribe Lead and Design Lead. Which tribe you'd lead is something we'll work out with you during the process.

This is a people leadership role with a hard technical requirement. The engineers report to you, so hiring, development, performance and pace are yours. At the same time you have to hold your own on system architecture: challenge estimates from your engineers, spar with the Product Tribe Lead on solutions, and know when a design is wrong before it ships. This role needs both.

HOW WE'RE SET UP

Tribes are the organisational body: people management, capacity, planning and reporting live there. Squads are assigned to problem spaces and run discovery and delivery, each led by a trio of Tech Lead, Product Manager and Product Designer. Tech Leads own the technical decisions in their squad, including estimates, and write code alongside their engineers. They don't manage people. You do.

We keep the structure deliberately flat. Management is anchored at tribe level, squad composition flexes to serve the most important work, and structure changes as we learn (roughly every six months in practice, not on a schedule). Discovery and delivery run in parallel: the next mission is scoped before engineers finish the current one, so engineers weigh in on architecture early and have the context to unblock themselves.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

- Feasibility and delivery for the tribe. You're accountable for tribe-wide delivery outcomes and velocity: the right problems, solved at the right quality, as fast as possible.

- The people. 15 to 20 direct reports. Hiring, onboarding, expectations, feedback, development, compensation and promotion recommendations, and the tough calls that keep talent density high. Tech Leads feed you performance signals; the decisions and the conversations are yours.

- Technical judgement across squads. Broad understanding of the tribe's systems and how they fit into the wider Moss architecture. You challenge estimates and technical proposals from your engineers; you don't produce the estimates yourself.

- A seat in the tribe trio. Roadmap and planning input through a feasibility lens. You argue solutions and trade-offs with the Product Tribe Lead as a technical peer, and push back on scope and timelines when the engineering picture says so.

- Operating rhythm. How the tribe plans, estimates, tracks and reports on delivery, with proactive, timely transparency to the tribe and to leadership, the good and the bad.

- Capacity. Putting your best people on the most impactful work, moving engineers between squads (and, where it serves Moss, between tribes) while still letting people build real domain depth.

- Alignment across tribes. Tribe leads aren't isolated trios. You align proactively with your peer Heads of Engineering and with platform and architecture owners, and you resolve shared-architecture questions through alignment, not around it.

HOW WE EXPECT LEADERS TO OPERATE

- Velocity first, with high agency. Working smart and hard on the right problems.

- Lead by example, stay close to the work. You know the details of what your team is building and course-correct in real time. You get hands-on when speed or quality is on the line.

title: Revenue Enablement Manager (m/f/d), Just-in-Time Enablement
description:
SoSafe has the ambition to become the leading human risk management provider in Europe. Our award-winning awareness platform triggers behavioural change by providing effective and engaging training and simulations on cybersecurity and data protection. Cybercrime is costing the world >$10 trillion annually and growing by 15% p.a. - we invite you to be part of the solution!

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every month, something new reaches our field teams from Product, Product Marketing and Marketing: a new use case, a fresh sales narrative, a campaign, a product update. Too often it arrives as a Slack post or a long deck, and sellers never really pick it up.

As Revenue Enablement Manager, Just-in-Time Enablement, you own that last mile. You are the front door between the teams who create news and the teams who use it, and you make sure every launch reaches Sales, Customer Success and Partnerships across Europe at the right time, in a format they can use in their next conversation.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Run the launch intake. Be the single entry point for PMM, Product, Marketing and others who want something to reach the field. Prioritize with clear criteria so sellers aren't overloaded.

- Own the field release calendar. Keep one view of what's coming, when, and for whom, shared with creators and sales managers.

- Turn launches into what sellers need. Shape each release into: what's new, who it's for, why customers care, how to talk about it, and how to handle the likely questions.

- Coach the creators. Brief PMM, Product and Marketing on what the field needs and review their materials before they go out. When the input is raw (specs, messaging docs, long decks), write the enablement content yourself: short, clear and practical.

- Deliver just in time. Pick the right format and moment: a 20-minute live session, a short recording, a one-pager, a talk track. Not so early it's forgotten, not so late it's useless.

- Make it stick. Run practice sessions, give managers simple talking points, and check that sellers can explain the new thing in their own words.

- Check it landed. Track attendance, usage in calls and deals, and rep feedback. Share what you learn with the creators so the next launch is better.

- Keep one home for launch material. Everything findable in one place with an owner and a review date; retire what's outdated.

- Hand over to curriculum. Work closely with your colleagues in the revenue enablement team, who fold a launch into the regular training once it is no longer new. Agree what moves over, when, and in what form, so nothing is built twice.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

- 5+ years in revenue enablement, product marketing, sales training or a similar role in B2B SaaS, ideally at a scaleup.

- Experience rolling out launches, messaging or campaigns to sales teams, with examples you can share.

- Ability to explain a product use case or sales narrative simply, and to spot what a seller really needs from it.

- Strong stakeholder skills: you can say "not this month", ask for a 3-slide version of a 40-slide deck, and keep the relationship strong.

- Well organized: you juggle several launches at once and hit dates.

- Clear writing and confident live facilitation.

- Hands-on with LMS, AI, video editing tools, a CRM and call recording tools, and a habit of using data to check adoption.

- Fluent English and German.

NICE TO HAVE:

- Background in product marketing or product management.

- Experience with security, compliance or HR-related products.

- Familiarity with a structured sales methodology such as SPICED or MEDDICC.

HOW SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

First 30 days: learn

- Meet the leads in PMM, Product, Marketing, Sales and Customer Success. Learn how launches reach the field today and where they get lost.

- Review the last 3-5 launches: what reached the field and what stuck.

- Agree which upcoming launches come first and who owns what, intake process and readiness gates.

Days 31-60: set up and pilot

- Start the launch intake

title: Python Software Engineer - Infrastructure & Platform
description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work-work that changes the world-is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

The role

Our Site Reliability Engineering team builds and maintains the core software, automation, and platform services that power engineering across Everpure. We approach reliability as a software problem: building developer tooling, automating complex operational workflows in Python, designing observable systems, and ensuring our internal platform scales seamlessly.

As a Python Software Engineer in Prague with a passion for infrastructure, you will write the software and tooling that keep our platform services reliable, scalable, and developer-friendly. You will collaborate closely with product engineering teams and platform developers across our global sites to automate infrastructure management and build self-healing systems.

What you'll do

Python Tooling & Infrastructure Automation:  Treat operations and infrastructure as software engineering problems. Design, build, and maintain Python-based automation, developer CLI tools, self-healing systems, and custom services that simplify deployment, monitoring, and platform operations.

Observability:  Help build and operate a consistent pipeline for metrics, logs and alerts across our data centres and public cloud. Improve detection speed and alert quality so that engineers are paged only when action is needed and have the context they need when they are.

Shared platform services: Operate the messaging, caching, database and continuous-integration services the platform depends on. Contribute to making them highly available: redundancy, capacity planning, upgrades and tested recovery procedures.

Automation:  Treat operations as an engineering problem. Build the tooling that removes repetitive work, from deployment and configuration automation to health checks and self-healing, and contribute to our work applying AI to incident triage and remediation.

Production readiness:  Take part in design and production-readiness reviews, capacity planning and launch support for new services, and help product teams adopt reliability practices so that fewer problems reach production.

We are primarily an in-office environment and therefore, you will be expected to work from the Prague office in compliance with Everpure's policies, unless you are on PTO, or work travel, or other approved leave.

What you bring

• Software engineering proficiency in Python, with experience building developer tools, backend services, or infrastructure automation.

• Hands-on experience operating distributed systems on Linux and Kubernetes using infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines.

• Strong troubleshooting skills across full-stack components, including networking, HTTP, containers, and storage.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills in English, with a strong emphasis on documentation and cross-team collaboration.

Our platform runs on Kubernetes across our own data centres and public cloud, and most of our tooling is written in Python and Go.

title: Senior IoT Engineer (all genders) – Embedded Linux · Python · Yocto
description:
Parking without barriers, tickets or queues. Wemolo builds its own hardware and its own AI to make that happen. More than 7,000 of our scanners run on around 4,000 parking sites across Europe and have processed over 1.3 billion parking events: unattended, outdoors, around the clock.

As Senior IoT Engineer (all genders), you join our Devices team and bridge both worlds: you own our Yocto-based Linux software platform and actively build the Python application services running on top of it. Python is your daily driver, but you go down to C/C++, drivers, and the kernel whenever hardware requires it. Neither pure BSP-only engineers nor high-level-only developers will be happy here - this is a true hybrid hands-on role.

Right now, we are building a new generalized Linux based platform for our next-generation hardware, harmonizing the software across all device types and making fleet health visible in real time. You do this in a profitable Munich scale-up with more than 250 people in five European locations: the pace of a fast-growing company and the stability to build things properly.

As we are looking for a hands-on developer, a live coding session is an integral part of our interview process.

WHAT TO EXPECT

- Next-Gen OS Image: Design and build our new Yocto-based Linux image for the next hardware generation, and drive the migration of our fleet onto it.

- Hardware Abstraction: Harmonize the software across scanners, payment terminals and screens into one maintainable codebase.

- Fleet Updates: Design OS and application updates that never brick a device: A/B partitions, staged rollouts and clean versioning across hardware variants.

- Fleet Observability: Build monitoring that shows the health of every device in real time, from memory leaks to network stability and hardware metrics.

- Debugging: Find root causes across kernel, drivers, networking, memory and application code, on devices hundreds of kilometers away.

- Technical Guidance: Bring senior judgment into architecture discussions with our IoT Platform, Backend and AI teams, document decisions and mentor engineers.

INSPIRE US BY

- Embedded Linux Expertise: Hands-on experience building and maintaining embedded Linux products that are deployed in the field, ideally at fleet scale, and confidence working with Linux internals, GNU tools, and Bash

- Background: Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or equivalent practical experience

- Yocto Experience: Proven experience building, customizing, and maintaining Linux images using Yocto

- Python Development: Strong Python skills - Python will be your primary development language in this role

- Systems Programming: Strong programming skills in at least one systems language such as C++, Rust, Go, or Java

- Operating System & Debugging: Solid understanding of Linux internals, bootloaders, systemd, drivers, kernel concepts, networking, and Docker, plus hands-on experience with debugging tools such as GDB, tcpdump, Valgrind, UART, and JTAG

- Senior Mindset: You clarify requirements before designing a solution, consider the impact on other teams, and are comfortable making and defending technical decisions

- Communication: You explain complex technical topics clearly and in a structured way, in fluent English (C1)

EXTRA POINTS FOR

- Experience operating large-scale IoT fleets

- Knowledge of industrial hardware, cameras, AI accelerators, modems, or network devices

- Experience with computer vision, edge AI, or machine learning

- Familiarity with MQTT and Protocol Buffers (ProtoBuf)

- German language skills

WHAT WE OFFER

- Flexibility & Responsibility: Your workday, your performance - Our hybrid model empowers you to focus from home, get fresh perspectives during workation, and connect in person during our Anchor Days (Tuesday to Thursday)

- Tailored Mobility: Full speed ahead - Whether it’s sustainable bike leasing or a public transport subsidy, we keep you flexible and on the move
